memory_update.text: ONTO should be treated as the reference/product-leader candidate for HBM4 inspection/metrology exposure, but not necessarily the most underfollowed name after public HBM4 selection evidence.
CAMT has direct advanced-packaging/HBM inspection evidence and remains in the preferred USD 300M-10B hunting band; verify AI/HBM order materiality and recurrence.
FORM is a plausible HBM probe-card/test bottleneck candidate; evidence is strong for technical relevance but needs revenue mix and customer proof before promotion.
KLIC is a lower-attention advanced-packaging equipment candidate with explicit HBM/high-density DRAM messaging around FTC and hybrid solutions; verify true HBM production adoption.
The cleanest sub-nodes for this Layer 1B pass are inspection/metrology, probe cards/wafer test, and thermo-compression/hybrid bonding equipment rather than headline HBM producers.

Later layers should check whether these names are already priced as HBM beneficiaries; the supplied search context warns that much of the sub-USD-50B HBM supplier layer may already be identified by the market.

CAMT should remain a high-priority Layer 2 candidate for HBM/advanced-packaging inspection because the gathered evidence includes explicit 2026 orders from a leading HBM manufacturer and tier-1 OSAT for AI-related applications.

FORM is a strong second-order probe-card candidate: its product evidence explicitly links HFTAP probe cards to HBM stack devices, fine-pitch interposers, known-good-die memory testing, and advanced packaging.
KLIC belongs in the advanced bonding subnode. Evidence supports HBM-adjacent memory bonding exposure, but production qualification with top HBM makers still needs verification.
ACMR is a speculative shadow candidate: evidence supports wafer-level packaging tools, but direct HBM/CoWoS/2.5D customer linkage is not yet proven and must be tested before promotion.

CAMT should remain in the underfollowed HBM/advanced-packaging discovery lane because its inspection/metrology tools have explicit HBM and advanced-packaging evidence, including order evidence tied to a leading HBM manufacturer.

FORM should remain in the underfollowed lane as a probe-card/test bottleneck candidate; HBM has already become a large portion of reported DRAM probe-card revenue, but margin and customer concentration must be checked.
KLIC is a higher-uncertainty HBM bonding-equipment hypothesis; evidence of a first HBM system is promising but needs revenue materiality, repeat-order, and customer-qualification verification.

AMKR is best used as a reference OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity anchor, not the core underfollowed idea, because its size and policy visibility make it less likely to be ignored than smaller tool and test suppliers.

The most important next verification gap is not whether these companies touch HBM, but whether HBM/advanced packaging is material enough to drive revenue, margins, backlog, and customer qualification durability.
CAMT should remain in the HBM/advanced-packaging second-order universe as an inspection/metrology supplier with explicit HBM, chiplet, hybrid-bonding, and AI-order evidence.
FORM should remain in the universe as a probe-card/test-intensity beneficiary where HBM complexity may increase wafer-test demand; verify customer concentration and HBM revenue materiality.
COHU is a lower-attention discovery candidate for HBM inspection/metrology and test handling; survival in later layers requires proof that Neon HBM selection is scaling into material revenue.

Need a separate pass on bonding, thermal-interface materials, substrates, and wet-process suppliers such as KLIC, ACMR, ONTO, and materials names; this pass prioritized stronger explicit HBM evidence in inspection, probe, and OSAT nodes.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe around HBM and advanced-packaging second-order suppliers. The strongest direct-exposure candidates in this pass are niche inspection/metrology, probe-card, and bonding-equipment vendors rather than the HBM producers themselves. The list deliberately avoids filling the universe with mega-cap AI or foundry anchors; ONTO is included as a niche reference/product leader, while CAMT, FORM, and KLIC form the underfollowed discovery lane. Market-cap buckets use live tool estimates as of 2026-06-13/14 and should be refreshed before later layers. Layer 1B expands the HBM/advanced-packaging equipment node with a bias toward US-listed, sub-$50B second-order suppliers. The highest-signal names in this pass are not HBM producers but vendors tied to inspection/metrology, probe cards, thermo-compression/hybrid bonding, and wafer-level packaging tools. Evidence strength is uneven: Camtek and FormFactor have explicit HBM-related product/order evidence; Kulicke & Soffa has explicit memory/HBM-adjacent advanced bonding evidence; ACM Research has advanced wafer-level packaging tool evidence but the direct HBM linkage remains a hypothesis to verify. Expanded the US-listed universe for the HBM and advanced-packaging second-order supplier node with a two-lane funnel: one reference packaging anchor and three underfollowed discovery candidates tied to probe cards, inspection/metrology, bonding, and advanced-packaging equipment. The main finding is that the cleanest underfollowed candidates are not obscure because HBM is hidden, but because their exposure sits one step
